name: Tenkubashi
tagline: Shinagawa in 31 minutes and Tokyo in 35 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Ota City, where Keikyu and Tokyo Monorail run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 40 minutes to Otemachi, 49 minutes to Shinjuku, 44 minutes to Shibuya and 31 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 3.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.4 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 3.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1 m to 3.4 m, a difference of 2.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 8 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 8 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: まいばすけっと 穴守稲荷店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 5 clinics and 3 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 渡辺病院, about 21 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 高野病院, about 21 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Keikyu Airport Line and Tokyo Monorail. The lines are split between operators (Keikyu runs 1 line and Tokyo Monorail runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Keikyu Airport Line and Tokyo Monorail. It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 2LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down.

neighbours.lead: Seibijo is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Tenkubashi is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Tenkubashi. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Tenkubashi.

neighbours.lead: Anamori-Inari is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is, but Tenkubashi is ahead on the number of lines and quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Tenkubashi. It takes 7 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Tenkubashi. One-room rents run about ¥6,000 higher.

leads.groceries: There are 2 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 10 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
